title: Telangana Launches QR Code Tool for HIV Risk Self-Assessment on Independence Day
excerpt: Starting August 15, Telangana residents can scan a QR code to privately assess their HIV risk, part of the state's push to eliminate HIV through technology-driven public health outreach.
body:
• Telangana will launch a QR code-based HIV risk self-assessment tool on August 15, allowing residents to privately evaluate their risk
  • The initiative is part of the state's broader goal to make Telangana HIV-free, building on a testing infrastructure that screened over 19 lakh people in 2024-25
  • Telangana's HIV positivity rate has dropped to 0.49% through targeted community-based testing strategies
  • Over 1.24 lakh people in the state currently receive free antiretroviral therapy through government-run ART centres

Telangana is set to roll out a QR code-based HIV risk self-assessment tool on August 15, Independence Day, in a move that blends digital innovation with public health outreach. The initiative will allow residents to scan a QR code and privately evaluate their HIV risk without visiting a clinic first — a significant step in reducing the stigma that still surrounds HIV testing in India.

How the QR Code System Works

The QR code, developed under the Telangana State AIDS Control Society (TGSACS), will link to a digital self-assessment questionnaire. Users can answer a series of questions about behavioural and clinical risk factors, receive an immediate risk evaluation, and get directed to the nearest Integrated Counselling and Testing Centre (ICTC) if further testing is recommended.

The tool is designed for smartphone access, making it available to a broad cross-section of the population. By removing the need for an initial in-person visit, health officials hope to reach people who might otherwise avoid testing due to fear of social stigma or a lack of awareness about their risk level.

Building on a Strong Testing Foundation

Telangana has already established itself as one of India's more aggressive states in HIV testing and treatment. In 2024-25, TGSACS tested more than 19.02 lakh people for HIV, identifying 9,415 positive cases. The state's HIV positivity rate has fallen to 0.49%, a three-fold reduction attributed to focused testing among high-risk groups and expanded community-based outreach.

Currently, over 1.24 lakh people living with HIV in Telangana receive free antiretroviral therapy through a network of government-run ART centres. Officials have identified 13 districts with more than 5,000 HIV patients each, and the state health minister has called for intensified testing across all 26 districts.

"The State government is committed to controlling HIV/AIDS completely by the year 2030."

— Telangana State Health Minister

Part of India's Broader Digital Health Push

The Telangana initiative aligns with a national trend toward technology-driven HIV prevention. The National AIDS Control Organization (NACO) has proposed deploying AI models to alert high-risk individuals, aiming to reach one lakh people by 2026. India's national HIV prevalence has declined from 0.33% in 2010 to 0.20% in 2024, with new infections dropping 49% over the same period — outpacing the global decline rate of 40%.

The QR code approach addresses one of the persistent barriers to testing: the first step. Even with free testing available at ICTCs across nearly every state, many people delay or avoid getting tested because of the perceived social cost of walking into a clinic. A private, phone-based risk assessment lowers that barrier.

What's Next

The QR code tool will go live on August 15 as part of Independence Day health awareness events across Telangana. Health officials plan to distribute the QR codes through government offices, hospitals, pharmacies, and public spaces. If the pilot succeeds, other states may adopt similar digital-first approaches to HIV risk screening as India pushes toward its 2030 elimination target.
nri_angle: Telangana's QR code initiative showcases India's growing digital health infrastructure, relevant to NRIs tracking healthcare innovation back home.
